body:
The fact that `InputEventKey` is triggered multiple times, is based on how operating systems (Windows/Linux/Mac/...) work: they send the key-pressed state once every few frames.
So Godot provides an additional functionality to check whether `InputEventKey` was pressed just now or if it is beeing held down:
``` gdscript
	if event is InputEventKey:
		if event.pressed and not event.echo:
			print("Key on keyboard pressed!")
```
By checking this `echo` property you can achieve the same functionality as with `InputEventMouseButton`.

On the other hand, the operating systems don't send mouse-button held down events, so Godot provides a different way to check for the state of the mouse-button:
``` gdscript
func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	if Input.is_mouse_button_pressed(MOUSE_BUTTON_LEFT):
		print("Process: mouse button pressed!")
```

So from a historical point of view, operating systems send multiple key-down events and only a single mouse-button-down event.
Godot just follows this decision, but also provides functionality to check the state of the mouse-button. I'm not seeing any need for changing this approach.

Also be aware that changing `InputEventMouseButton` to include an `echo`-property and sending it like keys once every few frames, would very likely break many existing projects, which depend on the current behavior: The current behavior is that Mouse-button-down is always followed by a Mouse-button-up and never by a second Mouse-button-down.

Interesting. Really didn't know it is because of operating systems. I still find it quite strange because intuitively this classes should have similar behaviour but your arguments seem legit. And now I agree that leaving everything as it is now is a right approach. Thanks for your explanation.
